verdicts.evidence: A phase becomes 'complete' as soon as ONE artifact is filled. MEASURED RECIPES (3 surfaces): (1) scaffold + filled framing.md, blank mission-contract.md (fxsome): check 'Current gate 1 · Frame' -> '2 · Architect' and check --json currentGate likewise — the ADR-0030 machine contract an agent follows sends it to the wrong phase, and the open steering contract drops out of the 'current gate' perimeter; (2) example mission + decision-matrix below the floor (fxws): the mutant prints 'Current gate all gates passed' NEXT TO '1 deliverable(s) not filled', exit 1 — the header contradicts the verdict in the same output; (3) mission where every phase has one filled artifact and none is complete (fxsome2, 10+ blank deliverables): status goes from '▸ 1 · Frame ← you are here' to 'Current gate iterate — steady-state (delivery arc complete)' + '▸ Iterate — continuous improvement ← you are here' — steadyState lies about the whole arc. The exit codes do not move (gaps are counted per artifact in countGaps, independently of complete) — and that is exactly why nothing sees it: VERIFIED by replaying the 7 legs, all PASS; smoke only asserts the steady-state wording on the fully filled example mission, where some==every; audit-corpus only judges exit codes.

The 'ADRs N' line of check and the adrCount field of --json lie with a zero on every real mission. KILLED BY THE SMOKE LEG, VERIFIED by replaying it: exit 1, assertion 'an ADR whose name contains 0000 (10000-ms) is counted, not dropped (mission/status/conformance agree)' (smoke.js:457, /ADRs\s+1\b/ on a scaffold mission carrying ADR-0021-timeout-10000-ms.md — the mutant prints 'ADRs 0'). The 6 other legs pass (adrCount is advisory, never in gaps).
